title: Rational strict feasibility for symmetric matrix equations
statement: Use the rational and real fields $\mathbf Q,\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field]. Let $n,m\geq0$ be integers. For $F=\mathbf Q$ or $\mathbf R$, let $\operatorname{Sym}_n(F)$ be the vector space of matrices $A=(A_{ij})_{1\leq i,j\leq n}$ with entries in $F$ and $A_{ij}=A_{ji}$. A real symmetric matrix is called positive definite if $\sum_{i,j}z_iA_{ij}z_j>0$ for every nonzero $z\in\mathbf R^n$. Let $L:\operatorname{Sym}_n(\mathbf Q)\to\mathbf Q^m$ be a $\mathbf Q$-linear map and let $b\in\mathbf Q^m$. Write $L_{\mathbf R}:\operatorname{Sym}_n(\mathbf R)\to\mathbf R^m$ for the real linear map with the same rational coefficients: use the basis matrices $E_{ii}$ and $E_{ij}+E_{ji}$ for $i<j$ on the source and the coordinate basis on the target, where $E_{ij}$ has a single entry $1$ at $(i,j)$ and all other entries zero. If there is a positive definite $G\in\operatorname{Sym}_n(\mathbf R)$ such that $L_{\mathbf R}(G)=b$, where $b$ is included coordinatewise in $\mathbf R^m$, then there is $H\in\operatorname{Sym}_n(\mathbf Q)$ with $L(H)=b$ whose entrywise image in $\operatorname{Sym}_n(\mathbf R)$ is positive definite. Empty matrices and empty coordinate spaces are allowed.

source.place: Agent auxiliary for the split-real sum-of-squares argument: rational strict feasibility of the Gram-matrix equations. Milne II §1, proof of Lemma 1.3, printed pp.77–78 motivates the ambient finite rational algebra only; this matrix lemma is not asserted there. Agent proof recorded in report.md.

proof.text: If $n=0$, there is just one rational or real empty matrix. The premise says $b_{\mathbf R}=0$, hence $b=0$ coordinatewise by injectivity of $\mathbf Q\hookrightarrow\mathbf R$; its rational empty matrix solves the equations and is vacuously positive definite. Assume $n>0$. Index the $d=n(n+1)/2$ upper-triangular entries by $I=\{(a,b):1\leq a\leq b\leq n\}$. The coordinate map $c_F:\operatorname{Sym}_n(F)\to F^I$ and its inverse copy each off-diagonal coordinate symmetrically. They are inverse linear maps by inspection of entries, and commute with rational inclusion.

source.place: Agent auxiliary to the Gram-matrix argument for lem-sfb-split-real-algebra-positive-squares. Milne II §1, Lemma 1.3, printed pp.77–78 motivates the rational algebra setting only; it does not assert this linear-algebra lemma. The agent argument is recorded in report.md.

proof.text: Let $A$ be the $m\times d$ rational matrix whose column at $(a,b)$ is $L(E_{aa})$ if $a=b$ and $L(E_{ab}+E_{ba})$ if $a<b$. Expanding a symmetric matrix in this basis gives $L(S)=Ac_{\mathbf Q}(S)$ and $L_{\mathbf R}(S)=A_{\mathbf R}c_{\mathbf R}(S)$. Thus $c_{\mathbf R}(G)$ solves $A_{\mathbf R}x=b_{\mathbf R}$. Apply [lem-sfb-rational-linear-system-parametrization] and lift its $x_0,v_j$ to rational symmetric matrices $H_0,V_j$. We obtain $L(H_0)=b$, $L(V_j)=0$, and $G=(H_0)_{\mathbf R}+\sum_{j=1}^k t_j(V_j)_{\mathbf R}$ for real parameters $t_j$.

source.place: Agent auxiliary to the Gram-matrix argument for lem-sfb-split-real-algebra-positive-squares. Milne II §1, Lemma 1.3, printed pp.77–78 motivates the rational algebra setting only; it does not assert this linear-algebra lemma. The agent argument is recorded in report.md.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-positive-definite-entrywise-neighbourhood] to the given real symmetric positive definite $G$, obtaining $\varepsilon>0$. If $k=0$, the preceding equality already makes $H_0$ a rational positive definite solution, so return $H_0$. Otherwise put $B=1+\sum_{j=1}^k\sum_{a,b=1}^n |(V_j)_{ab}|$ with rational entries viewed in $\mathbf R$, and $\delta=\varepsilon/B>0$.

source.place: Agent auxiliary to the Gram-matrix argument for lem-sfb-split-real-algebra-positive-squares. Milne II §1, Lemma 1.3, printed pp.77–78 motivates the rational algebra setting only; it does not assert this linear-algebra lemma. The agent argument is recorded in report.md.

proof.text: For each of the finitely many parameters $t_j$, apply [lem-sfb-real-rational-interval-density] to $t_j-\delta<t_j+\delta$ and choose $q_j\in\mathbf Q$ in that interval. Hence $|q_j-t_j|<\delta$. Set $H=H_0+\sum_j q_jV_j$. It is rational and symmetric, and linearity gives the exact rational equality $L(H)=L(H_0)+\sum_jq_jL(V_j)=b$.

source.place: Agent auxiliary to the Gram-matrix argument for lem-sfb-split-real-algebra-positive-squares. Milne II §1, Lemma 1.3, printed pp.77–78 motivates the rational algebra setting only; it does not assert this linear-algebra lemma. The agent argument is recorded in report.md.

proof.text: Entrywise the parameter expression for $G$ gives $H_{\mathbf R}-G=\sum_j(q_j-t_j)(V_j)_{\mathbf R}$. For every $a,b$, the triangle inequality gives $|(H_{\mathbf R}-G)_{ab}|\leq\sum_j|q_j-t_j||(V_j)_{ab}|\leq\delta\sum_j|(V_j)_{ab}|\leq\delta(B-1)<\varepsilon$, the last inequality following from $B\geq1$ and $\delta B=\varepsilon$. Since $H_{\mathbf R}$ is symmetric, [lem-sfb-positive-definite-entrywise-neighbourhood] now makes it positive definite. Together with the exact equation above this is the required $H$.
